newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela April inflation seen at 2.4 pct - report.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela April inflation seen at 2.4 pct - report.

text.p: Venezuela's inflation in April is expected to be around 2.4 percent, up from 1.6 percent in March, El Nacional newspaper reported on Wednesday.
Quoting Finance Ministry sources, the daily also said the inflationary impact of an increase in the minimum monthly wage would push inflation in May to between 3.5 and 4.0 percent.
That would be the peak for the year, it said, and the cost of living index would stabilize at around 2.0 percent per month from August and then drop to 1.5 percent towards the end of the year.
Inflation reached a record 103 percent in Venezuela in 1996 but has been steadily going down in recent months. March 1.6 percent was the lowest monthly level in five years.
The official 1997 target is 35 percent. Figures for April are expected to be released on Friday.

The government last month granted public servants a 75 percent wage increase and President Rafael Caldera was expected to announce on Wednesday new food and transportation bonuses for private sector workers, a move Central Bank officials have said will add some five percentage points to year-end inflation.
These decisions led International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus to warn last week of "disorderly and excessive wage pressure in view of the country's capacity."
